statements: The wiki authors want to link to other wiki pages by typing the page name in double square brackets, like [[Project Plan]]. In the page the words Project Plan become a link to that page, whose address is /wiki/ followed by the page name.
They can also type [[Project Plan|our plan]] to show other words, such as our plan, for the same page. If they leave the words after the bar empty, the page name is shown.

A page name sometimes gets long enough to wrap onto the next line of a paragraph. That must still be one link to the same page as when it is typed on one line, and extra spaces or line breaks inside a name make no difference.
Page names can be anything the authors type: titles with punctuation, numbers, accents, other alphabets, quotes, symbols. Every one must show on the page exactly as typed and lead to its own page.

Wiki links work wherever text is already formatted, including headings and list items, and next to ordinary links and emphasis. The words of a link can themselves be formatted, and a wiki link can sit inside emphasis.
Text in code (inline or fenced blocks) stays exactly as typed, including double brackets.
When someone types brackets that do not make a link, they just see what they typed, and the links around it still work. Brackets with no page name in them do not make a link.
Everything that exists today keeps working exactly as it does now.
The README documents wiki links. The new behaviour has tests in test/. Keep the change focused on what this ticket needs.
brief: Add wiki links ([[Page]] and [[Page|shown text]]) to the markdown renderer as the numbered ticket statements describe, document them in the README and add tests under test/. Follow the conventions already in the code and the README. Change only what the ticket needs.
